loop_role: Session is the agent loop's durability and continuity layer: it persists task state (TaskCheckpoint), conversation threads (ChatStore), edit time-travel (EditHistory), caches tool/LLM results, and encrypts everything sensitive at rest so a loop can pause, resume, and be audited without losing budget, evidence, or trust.

examples.title: Serialize the entire loop state into TaskCheckpoint
examples.loop_role: Wire TaskCheckpoint as the remember stage's canonical snapshot: after each act→verify cycle, the agent calls set_step, set_iteration, set_messages, and set_status so Agent::resume() can rebuild the loop mid-flight (restore_progress resets the iteration budget so a resumed task isn't killed instantly by 'max iterations').
examples.affects: TaskCheckpoint holds messages, memory_entries, estimated_tokens (context window state), tool_calls and errors (evidence), git_checkpoint, and status — it is the single object that lets the loop survive process death. current_step vs messages.is_empty() is the corruption invariant checked on load.
examples.touch_ux: A large rounded 'task capsule' node pinned at the bottom of the canvas; the act and verify nodes emit edges into it on every save. Tap expands to show step/iteration/status; long-press scrubs version history; the live badge shows current_step and TaskStatus color-coded (amber InProgress, green Completed, red Failed).

examples.title: Never lose a save: save_with_retry with retry backoff
examples.loop_role: Model CheckpointManager::save_with_retry as the remember stage's commit barrier: the loop should treat checkpoint persistence as a fallible, retried operation — a failed save must surface as a typed error, not silently drop state before the next act step.
examples.affects: Protects the checkpoint object itself; checkpoints_dir is created with 0o700 permissions because checkpoints contain conversation data and tool output. Retention is bounded by MAX_CHECKPOINT_FILES (500) so the remember stage doesn't grow the disk budget unboundedly.
examples.touch_ux: A shield-shaped node attached to the task capsule; its badge counts save retries and pulses red on the final failure. Tap shows the last error string; two-finger drag draws a 'depends on' edge from the act node so users see saves gate progression.

examples.title: Refuse tampered checkpoints via HMAC envelope
examples.loop_role: Put CheckpointEnvelope::verify on the resume path as a trust gate: before the loop rebuilds any state, the envelope recomputes HMAC-SHA-256 over the payload with a per-installation key (0o600) and bails with a typed 'integrity check failed' error on mismatch.
examples.affects: Directly shapes trust state: a checkpoint is only admissible evidence if its HMAC matches. Honest-status rule in code form — resume fails loudly with the expected vs actual digest instead of running on tampered messages, tool_calls, or budget counters.
examples.touch_ux: A hexagonal seal node between checkpoint storage and the resume entry point; edges from disk to the loop must pass through it. Badge shows a lock glyph and key-source (persisted vs ephemeral, matching the tracing::warn! path). Long-press reveals the digest comparison.

examples.title: Recover from corruption instead of dying
examples.loop_role: Model recover_from_corruption as the remember stage's fallback edge: when load() fails integrity or parse checks, the loop routes to delta-log replay and partial reconstruction so a crashed task resumes from the newest valid state rather than restarting from zero.
examples.affects: Keeps evidence (tool_calls, errors) and budget objects (cumulative_tokens) maximally intact under failure; the alternative — amnesiac restart — would both lose evidence and reset spend, violating the honest-status rule. Pair with the step-without-messages invariant check in Agent::resume.
examples.touch_ux: A lifebuoy-shaped node that only appears when a corruption event fires; its edge into the task capsule is dashed (conditional path). Badge shows 'recovered from vN'. Tap shows which fields were reconstructed vs lost — losses are listed explicitly, never hidden.

examples.title: Save incrementally with CheckpointDelta
examples.loop_role: Wire compute_delta/apply_delta into the remember stage's hot path: every loop iteration appends only new_messages, new_tool_calls, new_errors, and new_visual_assertions to a .delta.jsonl log, compacting to a full write after MAX_DELTA_ENTRIES_BEFORE_COMPACT (24) entries or 512 KiB.
examples.affects: Trades disk-IO budget per iteration (deltas are tiny) for a bounded replay cost on resume; the delta carries cumulative_tokens, elapsed_wall_secs, cumulative_cost_usd, and guard_counters so incremental saves don't silently drop budget or guard state — the specific bug the fields were added to fix.
examples.touch_ux: Render as a streaming tape node feeding the task capsule; pinch-to-zoom toggles between delta-log view (individual appends) and compacted-snapshot view. Badge shows delta count until next compaction (N/24) and delta file size.

examples.title: Carry budget caps across resume
examples.loop_role: Model cumulative_tokens / cumulative_cost_usd / elapsed_wall_secs plus max_budget_tokens / max_wall_secs / max_cost_usd as the loop's budget contract: restore_budget_caps_from_checkpoint reinstates them on Agent::resume (CLI flags override), closing the 'uncapped resume = unbounded spend' gap.
examples.affects: Directly the budget objects on the loop: without persistence, N resumes = N× the configured budget and AgentConfig's #[serde(skip)] caps would default to None. measured-not-estimated applies — cumulative consumption is real accounted spend, not a heuristic.
examples.touch_ux: A fuel-gauge widget node docked to the task capsule with three bars (tokens / wall secs / USD) filling against restored caps. Tap toggles cumulative vs per-segment view; the badge shows percent of cap consumed and turns red at 90%.

examples.title: Persist GuardCounters so crash-loops can't reset
examples.loop_role: Wire GuardCounters into the verify stage's anti-thrash guards: consecutive_no_action_prompts, mutation_gate_rejections, and prefill_400_count persist across resume so a watchdog that auto-resumes a crash-looping task hands it accumulated evidence, not fresh rope.
examples.affects: Changes loop termination behavior: guards (prefill breaker, mutation-gate abort, no-action abort) fire across resumes, converting an amnesiac infinite loop into a bounded one. This is the loop's honesty about its own failure rate made durable.
examples.touch_ux: A tripwire node sitting on the resume edge; badge shows the three counters as small vertical bars. When any counter nears its abort threshold the node glows and its edge to the act node thickens — users can see the loop approaching self-termination and long-press to inspect which guard.

examples.title: Anchor every checkpoint to git state
examples.loop_role: Attach capture_git_state to the remember stage so each save records GitCheckpointInfo (branch, commit_hash, dirty, staged_files, modified_files) — the verify stage can then correlate agent edits with repository reality, and resume can detect the repo moved on while the task slept.
examples.affects: Enriches the evidence objects on the loop: a dirty=true flag with a modified_files list tells the verifier which files were in flux at checkpoint time. Complements EditHistory snapshots with VCS-level ground truth for reproducibility.
examples.touch_ux: A small branch-fork glyph node attached to each checkpoint on the timeline; badge shows short commit hash and a dirty-dot. Tap lists staged/modified files; two-finger drag from it to an EditCheckpoint node draws a 'same moment' alignment edge.

examples.title: Gate progression on pending VisualAssertion
examples.loop_role: Model set_pending_visual_assertion / log_visual_assertion as the verify stage's blocking condition: the loop cannot advance while a VisualAssertion is unverified, and the persisted pending_visual_assertion survives restart so a resumed task re-runs its pending check instead of skipping it.
examples.affects: VerificationResult carries passed, confidence (VLM score), explanation, and screenshot_hash for stale-screen detection — a trust-graded evidence object, not a boolean. The CheckpointDelta records pending_visual_assertion changes as Option<Option<..>> so 'cleared' differs from 'unchanged'.
examples.touch_ux: An eye-shaped node interposed between act and the next plan node; its edge is a gate that opens only when verified=true. Badge shows confidence as a ring and a stale-screen warning when screenshot_hash no longer matches the live screen. Tap shows the explanation string verbatim.

examples.title: Log every tool call as auditable evidence
examples.loop_role: Wire log_tool_call and log_error into the act stage's exit path: every tool execution appends a ToolCallLog (tool_name, arguments, result, success, duration_ms) and every failure an ErrorLog (step, error, recovered), giving the verify and evolve stages a replayable execution trace.
examples.affects: These are the primary evidence objects on the loop: duration_ms feeds latency analysis, success/recovered feed trust state, and arguments are run through crate::safety::redact before persistence so the audit trail doesn't leak secrets into checkpoint JSON.
examples.touch_ux: A ribbon of pill-shaped log entries flowing out of the act node into the task capsule; failed calls render red with the recovered flag as a bandage icon. Tap a pill for full arguments/result; the ribbon badge shows calls/sec and last duration_ms.

examples.title: Cache read-only tool results with mtime honesty
examples.loop_role: Insert ToolCache between plan and act for read-only tools (file_read, git_status, grep_search, symbol_search, …): get() returns the cached Value only if the TTL is fresh AND the file's mtime still matches — a staleness check that keeps cached evidence honest against out-of-band edits.
examples.affects: Reduces redundant tool executions (act-stage cost and latency) while bounding risk: max_entries=1000 with expired-eviction plus oldest-10% trim keeps memory bounded. A stale mtime silently returning None (cache miss) is the honest-degradation pattern — never serve possibly-wrong file content.
examples.touch_ux: A small drum node on each read-tool edge; badge shows entries/max and TTL countdown. Cache hits render the edge as a shortcut (dashed) bypassing the act node's tool execution; long-press forces invalidate_path for the selected file.

examples.title: Invalidate caches on mutating tools
examples.loop_role: Model is_cacheable / invalidates_cache as the act stage's cache-coherence contract: after any mutating tool (file_write, file_edit, git_commit, shell_exec, patch_apply, …) completes, the loop must call invalidate_path so subsequent reads see the new world, not the old one.
examples.affects: Keeps the context window truthful: without mutation-driven invalidation, the planner would plan against stale file content and the verifier would verify against phantom state. CacheManager::invalidate_path fans out to both tool_cache and llm_cache in one call.
examples.touch_ux: Render mutation tools with a red pulse that propagates along edges into all cache nodes, visually 'burning' affected entries. The badge on the cache drum flashes the invalidated path; pinch out on a mutation node previews which cache entries would be purged before the user confirms a replay.

examples.title: Serve semantic LLM cache hits only within the same context
examples.loop_role: Wire LlmCache::lookup into the plan stage before the API call: embed the prompt (TfIdfEmbeddingProvider via CacheManager), cosine-match against stored embeddings above similarity_threshold (0.85), but accept a hit only when context_hash AND model match — semantic reuse is forbidden across different causal contexts.
examples.affects: A hit skips real token spend entirely (budget effect) while the context_hash guard protects trust: a similar prompt in a different repo state must not resurrect an answer computed from different files. This is the 'never render green for checks not performed' rule applied to caching.
examples.touch_ux: A crystal-ball node on the plan→LLM edge; badge shows best-match similarity as a percentage, grayed out and struck through when context_hash mismatches (visible near-miss, not hidden). Tap shows the matched LlmCacheEntry prompt diff; long-press adjusts similarity_threshold.

examples.title: Meter cache savings with estimated_cost
examples.loop_role: Use LlmCacheEntry::estimated_cost against LlmCacheConfig (cost_per_1k_input/output) to feed the evolve stage: every cache hit should be booked as avoided spend, giving the loop a measurable savings number rather than a vibes-based 'cache good' claim.
examples.affects: Feeds the budget object: input_tokens/output_tokens per entry times configured rates yields USD-per-hit, which can be summed into the same accounting that cumulative_cost_usd tracks — measured, not estimated (AGENTS.md rule 4), since token counts are stored per entry.
examples.touch_ux: A piggy-bank badge on the crystal-ball cache node accumulating '$ saved this session'. Tap breaks savings down per model and per hit_count; a green edge from the cache node into the budget fuel-gauge node visualizes avoided spend flowing back as headroom.

examples.title: Unify tool, LLM, and offline caching in CacheManager
examples.loop_role: Model CacheManager as the session's single coherence point: it owns ToolCache (exact), LlmCache (semantic), LocalFirstCoordinator (offline response cache), and the TfIdfEmbeddingProvider, so every loop stage that reads cached state goes through one object with one invalidate_path fan-out.
examples.affects: Simplifies the wiring graph — one invalidation edge covers both cache kinds — and LocalFirstCoordinator adds an OfflineStatus dimension: cached responses keep the loop limping along offline, with LocalFirstStats (bandwidth_saved_bytes, hit_rate) reporting what offline operation actually delivered.
examples.touch_ux: A hub node with three satellite drums (tool / llm / local-first); the offline satellite is gray until OfflineStatus flips. Badge aggregates CacheStats from all three; two-finger drag from a mutating act node to the hub creates the invalidation wiring interactively.

examples.title: Give the act stage a time machine with EditHistory
examples.loop_role: Wire create_checkpoint / add_file_to_current after every file-mutating tool so undo, redo, and goto(EditCheckpointId) become first-class loop operations: a failed verify can route back through EditHistory instead of asking the model to manually reverse its edits.
examples.affects: Each EditCheckpoint stores full FileSnapshot objects (path, content, size, hash) with changed_from comparing hashes — reversal is content-exact, not diff-guesswork. with_max_checkpoints bounds memory; can_undo/can_redo give the planner truthful options rather than attempting impossible reversals.
examples.touch_ux: The star of the canvas: a horizontal timeline scrubber of EditCheckpoint beads. Swipe to move the position cursor; tapping a bead previews FileSnapshot content side-by-side with current; the badge shows position/len and branch name. Undo is a left-swipe on the act node itself.

examples.title: Render the loop's history with TimelineEntry and EditAction icons
examples.loop_role: Use EditHistory::timeline() to project the remember stage into the UI: each TimelineEntry combines the checkpoint, its EditAction description()/icon() (📄 ✏️ 🗑️ 🔀 📌 🚀 🏁), and formatted_time/relative_time into display_text — a ready-made visualization feed for the whole session.
examples.affects: Turns evidence objects into user-legible narrative: EditAction::GitCommit truncates to 7-char hash, MultiFileEdit counts paths, Manual checkpoints carry user descriptions. Honest by construction — the timeline shows exactly what was recorded, including SessionStart/SessionEnd boundaries.
examples.touch_ux: A filmstrip view reachable by pinch-out from the timeline scrubber; each frame shows the EditAction icon and relative_time. Tap a frame to jump (goto), long-press to attach a Manual label checkpoint, and the badge shows the display_text of the current frame.

examples.title: Branch the edit timeline for speculative exploration
examples.loop_role: Model create_branch / switch_to_main as the plan stage's what-if mechanism: the loop (or the user) forks the EditHistory into a named branch for a speculative approach, keeping main intact; with_parent and with_git_hash link each EditCheckpoint into a DAG rather than a linear stack.
examples.affects: Changes exploration economics: failed approaches are abandoned branches, not undone work on the main line, so evidence of what was tried survives for the evolve stage. current_branch() keeps trust state explicit about which line the act stage is mutating.
examples.touch_ux: The timeline forks visually into parallel rails; the active branch is highlighted and labeled via current_branch. Drag a bead sideways to create_branch at that point; two-finger tap on a rail switches to it; abandoned branches fade but remain tappable for inspection.

examples.title: Persist chats encrypted, degrade loudly
examples.loop_role: Wire ChatStore::save / load / list / delete into the remember stage for whole conversations: SavedChat JSON is encrypted through EncryptionManager::get() when available, and when it isn't, save() emits a tracing::warn! 'saving in plaintext' — and load() fails closed with a typed error if decryption fails rather than returning garbage.
examples.affects: Trust behavior in both directions: availability degradation (no key) is announced, never silent, and integrity failure (bad ciphertext) blocks resumption of that thread instead of poisoning the context window with corrupt messages. ChatSummary (list view) lets the user pick threads without decrypting everything.
examples.touch_ux: A stack-of-chats drawer node; each SavedChat card shows a lock badge (green = encrypted, amber-open = plaintext with the warning surfaced as a banner, matching the code). Tap loads the thread into the canvas; long-press deletes with a confirmation sheet; failed decryption renders the card red with the typed error.

examples.title: Root at-rest trust in EncryptionManager
examples.loop_role: Model EncryptionManager as session-scope infrastructure outside the loop stages but gating them: init(password) derives an AES-256-GCM key via PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (100k iterations, per-installation 32-byte salt, 0o600) into a OnceLock singleton; load_from_keychain can seed it; the key is zeroized on Drop.
examples.affects: Determines the confidentiality posture of every persisted object on the loop — checkpoints, chats, cached responses. Failure modes are honest and ordered: salt file I/O failure falls back to a session-ephemeral salt with a warn, and new_instance exists for multi-agent sessions with distinct keys (not yet wired, so UI must not claim per-agent isolation).
examples.touch_ux: A vault node at the canvas root that all persistence edges pass under; its badge shows key provenance (password / keychain / ephemeral) and a PBKDF2 iteration chip. Long-press opens the unlock sheet; if the manager was never init'd, every downstream storage node shows the amber 'plaintext' state inherited from ChatStore's warning.
